Chapter 9: The Enduring Value of Fantasy in a Changing World
You know, in a world that seems to speed up every single day, it’s pretty easy to feel like fantasy just doesn’t fit anymore. There’s always homework to finish, chores that pile up, and endless screens competing for our attention. Real life pulls us in so many directions, it can be tough to find time for stories and imagination.
But here’s the thing—our need for fantasy doesn’t just disappear as we get older. It just changes shape.
For kids, fantasy is how they start to figure out the world around them. And for adults? Well, it can be a gentle reminder of the things that truly matter. Fairy tales and magical stories aren’t just for children. The lessons they teach, the images they paint, and that sense of endless possibility—they stick with us. They quietly shape how we see ourselves, and how we understand others.
Picture a teenager, standing at the edge of growing up, feeling lost or unsure of where they belong. The stories they loved as a child still have something to offer. Think about the hero’s journey, the battles with darkness, the hope for transformation—those themes never really go away, do they? No matter how old we get, they’re always relevant.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we lean on fantasy, even as adults. We dream about fresh starts, imagine better futures, and tell ourselves stories about who we are and who we might become. Fairy tales remind us that imagination isn’t just a nice-to-have—it’s essential. It keeps hope alive, even when things get tough.
There’s a certain comfort in knowing the stories we cherished as kids are still there, waiting for us. They offer reassurance when times are hard, spark inspiration when we’re filled with doubt, and give us a sense of being connected to something bigger than ourselves. In a world that can feel so uncertain, fairy tales are a gentle nudge, reminding us that anything is possible.
And that’s really the lasting magic of fantasy—it helps us look at the world with fresh eyes. It encourages us to keep asking questions, to imagine new possibilities, and to believe that change is always within reach. Whether you’re a child or an adult, fairy tales keep offering strength, hope, and a little bit of wonder—just when we need it most.
